messages:
grace: Quick sync — RFC follow-up on SDK surface. Two questions: (1) Python: separate SyncClient + AsyncClient vs single client that exposes both? (2) Retry & pagination: should we implement retries at the transport layer by default and keep pagination helpers in the client layer?

ben: +1 for separate Sync/Async in Python. Simpler ergonomics and avoids hidden asyncio shims. Typing is cleaner.

carla: I agree with ben. Sync users shouldn't pay the async plumbing. Also separate clients make it explicit which deps you pull.

anish: For transports: my proposal is transport-default retries (configurable on creation) + allow per-call overrides. That keeps a single place for backoff logic and central metrics. Pagination helpers stay in client surface (iterators/async iterators) because they vary by method semantics.

emily: can you sketch minimal API shapes? small code examples help decision.

grace: sure — rough sketches. Python (separate clients):
```python
# transport config created once, injected into both clients if needed
transport = HttpTransport(retries=RetryPolicy(backoff="exponential", max_attempts=4))
# sync client
sync = RedwoodSyncClient(transport=transport)
resp = sync.list_items(page_size=100)
for p in resp:
    handle(p)

# async client
async_client = RedwoodAsyncClient(transport=transport)
async for item in async_client.list_items(page_size=100):
    await process(item)
```

TS (single client — everything async):
```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({ transport: new FetchTransport({ retries: { maxAttempts: 3 } }) })
for await (const item of client.listItems({ pageSize: 100 })) {
  handle(item)
}
```

grace: note: in Python the transport is sync or async specific. We can offer two transport implementations but same RetryPolicy semantics.

ben: question on pagination tokens: should tokens be opaque strings or structured objects? Opaque is easier for us (we can change internals).

carla: prefer opaque tokens. If we ever change cursor encoding we avoid breaking clients. Expose helpers to parse only when absolutely necessary.

anish: also: telemetry. If retries live in transport, we can emit consistent retry metrics across languages. Good for cost analysis.

emily: edge case: library consumers wanting fine-grained idempotency control per method — per-call override solves it. e.g., `client.list_items(..., retry: { maxAttempts: 0 })`

grace: suggested decision (so we can lock down RFC):
- Python: provide RedwoodSyncClient and RedwoodAsyncClient.
- TS & Go: single client (language defaults make this natural).
- Retries: transport-level defaults with per-call overrides. Transport emits retry metrics.
- Pagination: client-level helpers (sync iterator + async iterator); tokens opaque.

carla: sounds good. I'll draft the RFC update and add examples.

devops-bot: :white_check_mark: sdk-spec-rfc.md updated in docs repo by @carla — link: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/sdk-spec-rfc

ben: minor nit: call the per-call override arg `retryOptions` or `requestOptions`? I prefer `requestOptions` to house other per-call knobs.

grace: agree. `requestOptions` seems more extensible. I'll update the RFC note.

emily: ok from me. +1

anish: +1. I'll add transport metrics instrumentation in the infra ticket.

grace: thanks all — Carla, can you open the PR with the updated examples? I'll mark RFC as accepted after that. :tada:
